title: An integral ring map does not raise Krull dimension
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map of commutative rings such that $B$ is integral over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] (every element of $B$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of $A$). Then $\dim B\le\dim A$ (Krull dimensions [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]: suprema of lengths of chains of prime ideals), and every maximal ideal of $B$ lies over a maximal ideal of $A$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OJ (lemma-integral-dim-up, line 27348) and its proof (Lemmas Tag 00GT integral-no-inclusion and 00OI going-up-maximal-on-top); used in the proof of Lemma Tag 032D ('Since $\dim(R)=\dim(R_0)$ this implies that $R_0\to R$ is injective')

proof.text: ($\dim B\le\dim A$.) Write $\varphi:A\to B$ for the ring map. Let $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\mathfrak q_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_n$ be a chain of prime ideals of $B$ of length $n$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and put $\mathfrak p_i=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)$. Each $\mathfrak p_i$ is a prime ideal of $A$: $1\notin\mathfrak p_i$ since $\varphi(1)=1\notin\mathfrak q_i$, and $ab\in\mathfrak p_i$ gives $\varphi(a)\varphi(b)\in\mathfrak q_i$, so $\varphi(a)\in\mathfrak q_i$ or $\varphi(b)\in\mathfrak q_i$. Since $B$ is integral over $A$ and $\mathfrak q_{i-1}$ is a prime with $\mathfrak q_{i-1}\subsetneq\mathfrak q_i$, incomparability [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability] gives $\mathfrak p_{i-1}\subsetneq\mathfrak p_i$ for $i=1,\dots,n$. So $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ is a chain of prime ideals of $A$ of length $n$, and $n\le\dim A$. Taking the supremum over all chains in $B$ gives $\dim B\le\dim A$ (if $B=0$ there is no chain and $\dim B=-\infty$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OJ (lemma-integral-dim-up, line 27348), proof: 'Immediate from Lemma 00GT (lemma-integral-no-inclusion) ... and the definitions' (Definition Tag 00KE)

proof.text: (Maximal ideals lie over maximal ideals.) Let $\mathfrak n\subset B$ be a maximal ideal. Since $B$ is integral over $A$, $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)$ is a maximal ideal of $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal]; that is, $\mathfrak n$ lies over the maximal ideal $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)$ of $A$.
